claims.text: Abx in the catarrhal stage help; once paroxysms start they have limited effect but are still given to limit spread.
claims.quote: Antibiotics given during the catarrhal stage have been found to help ameliorate the disease. After paroxysms are established, antibiotics have been found to have a limited clinical effect but are recommended to limit spread.

claims.text: Preferred: erythromycin for 14 days or azithro for 5 days;
claims.quote: Preferred antibiotics are Erythromycin for 14 days Azithromycin for 5 days

claims.text: infants ≤ 6 wks: azithro preferred (erythromycin ↑ risk of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis);
claims.quote: Azithromycin is preferred in infants ≤ 6 weeks old because erythromycin has a higher risk of infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis

claims.text: ≥ 2 mo and macrolide-intolerant or hypersensitive: TMP-SMX may be substituted.
claims.quote: Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole may be substituted in patients ≥ 2 months old who are intolerant of or hypersensitive to macrolide antibiotics.
